Moving Window Estimation

Source: R/nonlinear.R
ivmw.Rd

ivmw() fits an IV estimator in moving (sliding) windows of consecutive observations ordered by the first stage residuals (equivalently by the IV-free exposure), to explore whether the causal effect varies with the level of the exposure, as described by Burgess et al. (2014). It is the equivalent of the ivmw prefix command in the Stata package ivonesamplemr.

Usage

ivmw(
  formula,
  instruments,
  data,
  estimator = ivreg::ivreg,
  window,
  step = 1,
  par = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'ivmw'
print(x, digits = max(3, getOption("digits") - 3), ...)

# S3 method for class 'ivmw'
plot(
  x,
  xlab = "Median of exposure in moving window",
  ylab = "Estimated causal effect",
  ...
)

Arguments

formula, instruments

formula specification(s) of the model, as for the estimator, with a single exposure, e.g. y ~ x + w | z1 + z2 + w.

data

a data frame containing the variables in the model.

estimator

the function used to fit the model within each group, e.g. ivreg::ivreg(), msmm(), lsmm(), tsps(), or tsri(). It must accept formula and data arguments and return an object with coef() and vcov() methods.

window

the number of consecutive observations in each window.

step

the number of observations by which successive windows are moved.

par

the name of the parameter to collect from each fit. By default the parameter of the exposure, which is the causal effect on the scale on which it is estimated, for example the log causal risk ratio for msmm().

...

further arguments passed to estimator, e.g. link for tsps() and tsri() or estmethod for msmm().

x

an object of class "ivmw".

digits

the number of significant digits to use when printing.

xlab, ylab

axis labels.

Value

An object of class "ivmw", a data frame with one row for each window and the columns start and end (the first and last observation of the window in the ordering by the first stage residuals), n, beta, se, medexposure, lowci, and uppci, as for ivxtile(). The object has print() and plot() methods.

Details

The first stage linear regression of the exposure on the instruments and any covariates is fitted in the full data, and the observations are ordered by its residuals. The estimator is then fitted in windows of window consecutive observations, starting at observations 1, 1 + step, 1 + 2 step, and so on. With the default step = 1 there are n - window + 1 windows, as for Stata's ivmw command.

The approach relies on the same additional assumption as ivxtile(), that the effect of the instruments on the exposure is the same in each window (Burgess, 2023).

References

Burgess S, Davies NM, Thompson SG. Instrumental variable analysis with a nonlinear exposure-outcome relationship. Epidemiology, 2014, 25, 6, 877-885. doi:10.1097/EDE.0000000000000161

Burgess S. Violation of the constant genetic effect assumption can result in biased estimates for non-linear Mendelian randomization. Human Heredity, 2023, 88, 1, 79-90. doi:10.1159/000531659

See also

ivxtile()

Examples

set.seed(12345)
n   <- 5000
z   <- rbinom(n, 2, 0.3)
u   <- rnorm(n)
x   <- 0.5 * z + u + rnorm(n)
y   <- 0.5 * x + 0.2 * x^2 + u + rnorm(n)
dat <- data.frame(y, x, z)
res <- ivmw(y ~ x | z, data = dat, window = 2500, step = 250)
res
#> 
#> Estimates of x in moving windows of the first stage residuals:
#> 
#>  start  end    n   beta      se medexposure  lowci  uppci
#>      1 2500 2500 0.3113 0.07918    -0.67168 0.1561 0.4665
#>    251 2750 2500 0.4138 0.07621    -0.46808 0.2644 0.5632
#>    501 3000 2500 0.5580 0.07234    -0.27253 0.4163 0.6998
#>    751 3250 2500 0.6412 0.07162    -0.06634 0.5008 0.7816
#>   1001 3500 2500 0.6930 0.07147     0.13194 0.5529 0.8330
#>   1251 3750 2500 0.8123 0.06963     0.31071 0.6758 0.9487
#>   1501 4000 2500 0.8352 0.07041     0.47866 0.6972 0.9732
#>   1751 4250 2500 0.8634 0.07061     0.65569 0.7250 1.0018
#>   2001 4500 2500 0.9563 0.06897     0.84681 0.8211 1.0915
#>   2251 4750 2500 1.0507 0.06867     1.05877 0.9161 1.1853
#>   2501 5000 2500 1.1288 0.07326     1.26509 0.9853 1.2724
#> 
plot(res)
